summary: Background check company exposed 2.9 billion records including Social Security numbers, names, and addresses. The breach led to the company's bankruptcy and cessation of operations in October 2024.

Massive dataset containing 26 billion records compiled from 3,876 websites, including LinkedIn, Twitter, Adobe, and Dropbox. Also included government organizations from US, Brazil, Germany, and other countries.

Largest breach in US history exposed Social Security numbers and health records of 26 million Americans. Safepay ransomware group claimed responsibility, obtaining over 8 terabytes of data from this healthcare payment processor.

Hackers stole call and text records from AT&T's workspace on a third-party cloud platform. Affected nearly all wireless customers and MVNO users. AT&T paid attackers $370,000 ransom to delete stolen data.
Unauthorized access to a cloud database hosted by third-party provider Snowflake. Exposed email addresses, phone numbers, and encrypted credit card information of North American customers.
Part of the Snowflake campaign where hackers stole terabytes of data from 165 organizations. Affected millions of customers with personal data exposure.

320GB of logs containing 120 million records exposed online since August 2025. Included cookies, timestamps, and identifiers affecting Fortune 500 companies including US Bank, Ford, GM, and BMW dealerships.
